title: Recorded Conversations - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille
text: Recorded Conversations - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Our Courses Train Your Team Articles Just Now Possible Get in Touch Sign in Subscribe Recorded Conversations - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Teresa Torres 06 Oct 2026 13 min Listen to this episode on: Spotify | Apple Podcasts We now record almost everything — every meeting has an AI note-taker, and some people wear glasses that capture every word. So what does that do to our relationships when nothing is forgotten and everything can be fact-checked? Petra Wille and Teresa Torres explore the promise and the unease of a fully-transcribed world. Teresa shares how checking her own Granola transcripts revealed she'd been misremembering conversations — and getting frustrated with people over things she never actually said. Petra describes the strange feeling of a colleague pulling up a transcript to correct her recollection of her own past opinion. Together they get to the bigger question: should we hold people accountable to what they said weeks ago, or grant each other permission to evolve? Key Takeaways Your memory is not a recording — Teresa's transcripts repeatedly showed her that her confident recollections didn't match what was actually said. Use it on yourself first. Checking your own transcripts to spot blind spots feels very different from having someone use them against you. Give people permission to evolve. What someone said three weeks ago matters far less than what they think now. The same record can be a collaboration tool or a weapon — the difference is intent and the permission to change your mind. Notes ≠ transcript ≠ truth. Each layer adds interpretation, so don't build a conversation on a record you haven't verified. Pull Quotes "My perception of reality is not the same as reality." — Teresa "Why does it matter what you might have said three weeks ago? Doesn't it matter more what you think now?" — Teresa "We need to grant each other the right of evolved opinions." — Petra "My brain just made up a whole new t-shirt that does not exist in the world." — Teresa Resources & Links: Follow Teresa Torres: https://ProductTalk.org Follow Petra Wille: https://Petra-Wille.com Mentioned in this episode: Meta smart glasses — recording wearables, discussed with some healthy skepticism (Petra hates them btw) Granola — the AI meeting note-taker Teresa uses for her one-on-ones Tab Benoit — the musician behind the infamous phantom t-shirt Become a Better Product Leader: A 52-Week Transformation Journey — Petra’s email course Chris Argyris — his work on action science (Action Science: Concepts, Methods, and Skills for Research and Intervention) is cited as a root of adult development research Loevinger's stages of ego development by Jane Loevinger , who is a developmental psychologist known for her stages of ego development Theory of mind Join the Conversation: Have thoughts on this episode?
